2013 Specialists Agreement: The AMA Victoria – Victorian Public Health Sector - Medical Specialists Enterprise Agreement 2013.
2018 Specialists Agreement: The AMA Victoria – Victorian Public Health Sector - Medical Specialists Enterprise Agreement 2018-2021.
Act: The Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth), as amended or replaced from time to time.
Agreement: The Medical Specialists (Victorian Public Health Sector) (AMA Victoria/ASMOF) (Single Interest Employers) Enterprise Agreement 2022–2026.
Ambassador: An appointed representative of the Association.
Association: The Australian Medical Association (Victoria) Limited (AMA) or the Australian Salaried Medical Officers Federation (Victoria Branch) (ASMOF).
Clinical Academic: A Specialist employed in a full-time capacity by a University in an academic role in the faculty of medicine, who is also employed by a Health Service.
CME Support Entitlement: The amount of CME funding support a Doctor is entitled to in a Financial Year, calculated under subclause 41.1(a) (full-time) or 41.1(c) (fractional).
DH: The Department of Health, or its successor, however titled or styled.
Doctor: A medical practitioner employed by a Health Service as a Specialist or Executive Specialist on a full-time, fractional or internal locum basis; with respect to Dental Health Services Victoria, means only a Doctor employed as an Anaesthetist.
Doctors in Training Agreement: The Doctors in Training (Victorian Public Health Sector) (AMA Victoria/ASMOF) (Single Interest Employers) Enterprise Agreement 2022–2026.
Employee: Has the same meaning as Doctor.
Employer: Has the same meaning as Health Service.
Executive Specialist: A Doctor expressly appointed as an Executive Specialist who is required to exercise professional leadership and/or management accountability clearly outside the responsibility of other Specialists.
Fractional Doctor: A Doctor engaged on a fractional basis in accordance with subclause 16.2.
Full-time Doctor: A Doctor engaged on a full-time basis in accordance with subclause 16.1(a).
Health Service: A public hospital or health service listed in Appendix 1 of this Agreement.
Higher Qualification: A postgraduate degree, diploma, or membership/fellowship of a Specialist Medical College appropriate to the specialty in which a Doctor is employed.
HSR: Health and safety representative (including a deputy health and safety representative).
Institution: Any hospital, health service or benevolent home, community health centre, Society or Association registered pursuant to the Health Services Act, whether or not listed in Appendix 1.
Internal Locum: A Doctor engaged on a casual basis in accordance with subclause 16.4.
Portable Technological Aids: Easily portable items designed for use away from the Doctor's usual work site that can operate without an external power supply. Does not include capital items such as ultrasound imaging devices.
Private Practice Income: Income derived by a Doctor because of the exercise of private practice privileges, whether collected directly by the Doctor or through the Health Service acting as agent.
Regulations: The Fair Work Regulations, as varied from time to time, and any successor to those Regulations.
Shiftworker: For NES purposes, any Doctor required to work in excess of ordinary hours, or who works ordinary hours on more than 10 weekends during the leave accrual year.
Specialist: A Doctor who holds Specialist Registration with the Medical Practitioners Board of Australia, or who possesses a Higher Qualification appropriate to their specialty.
Specialist Medical College: A medical college accredited by the Australian Medical Council.
Specialty: A field of work requiring the application of special experience and qualifications in a particular branch of medicine.
Statutory Body: The Department of Health (Victoria), formerly the Department of Health and Human Services (Victoria).
VHIA: Victorian Hospitals' Industrial Association — the employers' representative body.
WIRC Act: Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 (Vic), or where applicable the Accident Compensation Act 1985 (Vic) or the Workers Compensation Act 1958 (Vic).
